headline: RU hall provost withdrawn after attack on journalists; probe ordered within 72 hours
summary: The provost of Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Hall at Rajshahi University has been removed from duty following an attack on journalists, with an investigation committee tasked to submit a report within 72 hours.
details: The provost of Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Hall at Rajshahi University has been withdrawn from duty due to alleged negligence following an attack on journalists. An investigation committee has been instructed to submit its report within 72 hours.
This decision was announced by the university's Vice-Chancellor late Tuesday night, around 2 AM, after a meeting with the protesting students and journalists.

Journalists and students staged a protest in front of the administrative building, condemning the university administration's decision to file a case against unnamed individuals regarding the attack. They gathered on Monday evening, chanting slogans against the administration and Chhatra Dal.
The protesters later held discussions with the Vice-Chancellor at 11 PM. Following assurances from the VC, the students announced a temporary suspension of their movement until Thursday evening.
caption:
A university hall provost has been removed from duty after an attack on journalists at Rajshahi University. An investigation report is due in 72 hours.

The provost of Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Hall at Rajshahi University has been withdrawn from duty due to alleged negligence following an attack on journalists. An investigation committee has been instructed to submit its report within 72 hours.

This decision was announced by the university's Vice-Chancellor late Tuesday night, around 2 AM, after a meeting with the protesting students and journalists.

Journalists and students staged a protest in front of the administrative building, condemning the university administration's decision to file a case against unnamed individuals regarding the attack. They gathered on Monday evening, chanting slogans against the administration and Chhatra Dal.

The protesters later held discussions with the Vice-Chancellor at 11 PM. Following assurances from the VC, the students announced a temporary suspension of their movement until Thursday evening.

Source: Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo, Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star

headline_marked: [[32 killed as Nigerian military plane crashes]] in Ondo state during routine mission
headline: 32 killed as Nigerian military plane crashes in Ondo state during routine mission
summary: A Nigerian military ATR-42 aircraft, carrying 25 passengers and seven crew, crashed in Ondo state, leaving no survivors. President Bola Tinubu has ordered a thorough investigation into the incident.
details: A Nigerian military plane crashed in southwestern Ondo state on Monday, killing all 32 people aboard, including 25 passengers and seven crew members. The aircraft was flying from Benin City to Lagos when it went down.

President Bola Tinubu confirmed there were no survivors, expressing profound sadness and offering condolences to the families of the victims. He has directed the Nigerian Air Force to immediately begin a thorough investigation into the cause of the crash.

Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo stated that air traffic controllers lost contact with the ATR-42 aircraft at 0813 GMT during its routine mission. The crash marks one of Nigeria's deadliest air disasters in recent years.
Wreckage was subsequently located near the coastal town of Igbokoda, where search and rescue teams were deployed. The investigation aims to prevent future incidents.
caption:
A Nigerian military plane crash has claimed the lives of all 32 people on board, including 25 passengers and seven crew members. The incident occurred in Ondo state during a routine flight.

A Nigerian military plane crashed in southwestern Ondo state on Monday, killing all 32 people aboard, including 25 passengers and seven crew members. The aircraft was flying from Benin City to Lagos when it went down.

President Bola Tinubu confirmed there were no survivors, expressing profound sadness and offering condolences to the families of the victims. He has directed the Nigerian Air Force to immediately begin a thorough investigation into the cause of the crash.

Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo stated that air traffic controllers lost contact with the ATR-42 aircraft at 0813 GMT during its routine mission. The crash marks one of Nigeria's deadliest air disasters in recent years.

Wreckage was subsequently located near the coastal town of Igbokoda, where search and rescue teams were deployed. The investigation aims to prevent future incidents.
